To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) oxidative stress, as well as heat shock and reperfusion, activates transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms, and (2) the pattern of gene induction and transcription-factor activation varies in relation to the mechanism by which oxidative stress is produced.
oxidative stress, as induced by three different chemicals, activates the transcription of the hsc 73 and of other genes, but not the transcription of the inducible heat-shock hsp 70 genes.
oxidative stress induces the expression of hsc 73 and of some other genes, but not that of hsp 70, which is induced by heat shock or post-ischaemic liver reperfusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of the expression of the genes involved in heat-shock response with those induced by oxidative-stress-inducing chemicals.
a differential response of genes involved in the cellular defence mechanisms, such as heat-shock and oxidative stress.
the activation of the hsp genes in oxidative stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oxidative stress caused by chemical agents induces the expression of a set of genes, including haem oxygenase and hsc 73, but does not activate the heat-shock response and does not promote HSF binding.
oxidative stress induces the expression of a number of genes that are also activated in heat-shock or reperfused livery.
the expression of the genes studied is differentially activated by oxidative stress and that the mechanisms of activation are different from those of post-ischaemic liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oxidative stress activates transcription factors that are not involved in heat-shock response, but are involved in the expression of genes related to growth and differentiation, and that oxidative stress activates a gene (hsc 73) that is not activated in the heat-shock response.

, although oxidative stress is a condition that can activate the expression of several genes, it is not sufficient to induce the expression and/or the binding to DNA of the heat-shocks and post-ischaemia transcription factors.
oxidative-stress-inducing chemicals do not activate the hsp 73/hsp 70 heat-shock response and do not induce the binding of HSPF (heat-shock factor) to HSE (heat-shock element).
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under conditions of oxidative-stress, there is a selective activation of genes involved in the response to stress, but not of genes induced by heat shock.

oxidative stress is a condition that activates the expression of genes that respond to oxidative stress but that is not sufficient, in itself, to activate the hsp 71 gene, whose expression is induced by other conditions such as heat shock and post-ischaemia.
the activation of the heat-shocked and of the oxidative-stress pathways in the liver are two different processes, which are regulated by different transcription factors.
